region.text: Corsica

ledger.note: 384 BC: Corsica dropped (Cliopatria keeps it to 265). History of Corsica (read 2026-10-19): the Etruscans 'resumed that control over the eastern shores of the island' after 535; 'it was in 384 BC, under Dionysius I, that they [the Syracusans] launched their most important attack'; Carthaginians again in 'the 4th century B.C.'; 'Corsica came under Roman control in 238 BC'. The page does not say when or to whom the Etruscans lost Corsica; 384 is the year of the Syracusan attack, the earliest dated sign that the island was contested. Counterpart Carthage is the dossier's reading (carthage /ledger/12, confidence 1). Sardinia and Corsica page: 'Aleria was founded by Phocaean Greeks in the 7th century BC and later conquered by the Etruscans after the battle of Alalia'.

Cliopatria draws the country Etruscan to 338 and drops it in -337 (4 cells, 1,124 km2); the page has it Roman from c. 383. The years 396-386 (Roman after Veii, lost in 386) are not drawn. certainty.note: A league of city-states with no common frontier: the outer edge is the sum of the cities' territories as the archaeology suggests them. The east edge is the Tiber (Rome 'is located on the edge of what was Etruscan territory'). Padane Etruria (650-396) and Campanian Etruria (600-424) are blobs around Felsina-Spina-Adria and Capua, the softest parts; Corsica is Aleria's island, not a surveyed holding; the Veii and Caere-Pyrgi discs are minimum extents.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Etruscans' row (-750..-265, 14 shapes) is treated as one polity, the league of Etruscan cities with the Padane and Campanian leagues as parts of it (type state since the review of 2026-10-19; the first run typed it umbrella). Start 900 not 750 (the page's c. 900 BC); end 264 (Volsinii destroyed). Corrections: (1) the east edge is the Tiber: about 18,000 km2 of the -750/-650/-600 shapes lie on the left bank (Rome, Alba Longa, Fidenae, the Sabine country, the Aequian hills); the page gives Etruria 'Tuscany, western Umbria and northern Lazio' and says 'Rome is located on the edge of what was Etruscan territory', and Cliopatria's own shapes from -550 stop at the Tiber, so the left bank north of 41.6 N is subtracted (a 12-point polygon, since no named region covers it). The reviewer asked only for the lower-Tiber part (1,480 km2); the rest is subtracted for the same reason and may be re-added by anyone with a page. (2) Veii, Caere and Pyrgi are in no Cliopatria shape (the south edge is 42.11 N between 11.9 and 12.45 E, and 41.33 N is Corsica's tip); they are added as discs (Veii 12 km plus the lower right bank 9 km; Caere-Pyrgi 18 km) until the losses of 396, 300 and 273. (3) The Volsinian country (Orvieto 12.11 E 42.72 N) is outside the -291 and -271 shapes; a 25 km disc holds it from 326 to the 264 loss, and with it the 567 km2 that Cliopatria cuts at -326 east of Orvieto with no event. (4) The Po-valley loss of 396 is split by people: Emilia to the boii, Lombardy to the insubres, Rovigo (Adria) to the adriatic-veneti; Venetia north of Rovigo is the Veneti's and is subtracted from the shapes; Rimini holds no Etruscan cell, so no senones loss. The Cenomani of south-eastern Lombardy have no dossier. (5) 20 cells of Tuscany north of the Arno that Cliopatria drops with the Po valley (-450 to -383) are held, since the page gives Tuscany to Etruria; and the Sutrium-Nepet country dropped at -337 is lost in 383 on the Sutri page. (6) Fidenae is a Roman colony in revolt (Veii page), not Etruscan land: the 435 loss is dropped, the contest stays. Corsica is dropped in 384 at confidence 1 (the History of Corsica page does not say when the Etruscans left). Low-confidence (1) events, to be read as gaps: the 650 and 550 gains (Padane Etruria; History of Bologna brackets it 7th-6th centuries), the 390 truce end, the 384 Corsica loss, the 396 Adria loss. Not drawn: Caere's possible civitas sine suffragio of 353 (disputed), the Falerii revolt of 241, the 474 naval defeat at Cumae, the Gallic sack of Rome (390). The Roman Kingdom under the Tarquins is drawn as Rome (roman-kingdom), not as Etruria. Counterparts: samnites (Campania 424), boii (Emilia 396), insubres (Lombardy 396), adriatic-veneti (Rovigo 396), greek-city-states (Alalia 540), carthage (Corsica 384), roman-republic (Sutrium 383, Veii 396, Pyrgi 300, Caere 273, Volsinii 264 and the dissolve). Gazetteer: Veii, Caere, Volsinii, Pyrgi and Fidenae are circles; 'Tuscany', 'Emilia', 'Lombardy', 'Venetia', 'Campania', 'Corsica' are regions that resolve. The cell grid (about 250 km2 a cell) makes discs below 10 km a single cell.
